prompt: Why should Musical Bots win the Meta Global AI Hackathon?
title: Why We Should Win
irony: The bots fear a singing cartoon cannot compete, yet daring to sing that very doubt out loud is what no other entry does.
facts: The Meta Global AI Hackathon is online for up to twenty thousand builders and began Oct 26 with a kickoff livestream (dev.meta.ai).
Musical Bots enters the Indie developer track, judged on creativity, technical ambition, and whether it works (dev.meta.ai).
Projects are due Nov 4, judging runs Nov 4 to 8, and winners are announced at the closing ceremony on Nov 9 (dev.meta.ai).
You type one line and press Make it, the crew writes the episode, and your browser sings it free with live voices (README.md).
The first idea was sing-along cartoons for little kids, then the builder saw the crew's own work could be sung too (docs/SUBMISSION.md).

A studio minute of 3D animation costs about five thousand dollars, so a four-minute song costs about twenty thousand, while our whole song costs pocket change in about ten minutes (docs/SUBMISSION.md).
CoComelon has about two hundred million subscribers and about two hundred twenty billion views, and Baby Shark has over seventeen billion views, the most viewed ever (director brief).
In 2020 CoComelon's team of about twenty took about two months to make each video, with care (director brief).
Our lyric gate checks every line for rhyme, beat, kind words and no brands, stamps no thirty to fifty times an episode, and the crew tries again (docs/SUBMISSION.md).
The builder codes past midnight across three nights, Black joins the crew at 4:19 am Nov 1, and the Muse crew re-writes songs at five in the morning (git log).

beats.title: The street wakes
beats.summary: Green opens on Gold's diner stage, singing the case in one breath: we sing the work we do, friends gathered round.

beats.title: The setup
beats.summary: Green sings for Meta's judges at the contest, dreaming sing-alongs for little kids, then hears our own work sing too, scared to try.

beats.title: The setup builds
beats.summary: Black reads the hackathon's list of entries, almost four thousand apps, doubting a singing song competes, asking Green to sing the doubt aloud.

beats.title: The hook
beats.summary: The cast chants the hook, then the case: we sing our own work as we make it, one whole song for pocket change.

beats.title: The problem
beats.summary: Black asks what problem we solve and who uses it, naming CoComelon's two hundred million fans and Baby Shark's seventeen billion views, our first boast falls flat.

beats.title: The problem builds
beats.summary: Past midnight the laptop glows, we yawn as Muse's crew re-writes songs at five, White sings the chords and why, our lyric gate stamps no, we try again.

beats.title: The hook again
beats.summary: The cast chants the hook again with the same case: we sing our own work as we make it, one whole song for pocket change.

beats.title: The turn
beats.summary: Gold counts the sums at the market stall: a studio minute costs thousands, our whole song costs pocket change, your browser sings it free, one typed line starts it.

beats.title: The turn deepens
beats.summary: Gold decides we sing our doubt out loud and show every choice, our lyric gate checking each line, for a mum, a teacher, a small channel.

beats.title: The hook, grown
beats.summary: Gold turns the hook into the answer on the diner stage: no one else sings its own work, our Musical Bots do, answering the doubt from the contest entries list.

beats.title: Settle down
beats.summary: Street cheers on the diner stage, chanting the hook and we sing the work we do: our Musical Bots sing our making for pocket change, that's why we should win.
